summary: This note is a general overview of entomology, the scientific study of insects as a branch of zoology, covering its definition, overlap with other scientific fields, and its history from prehistoric agriculture-linked roots through early modern natural history to professionalization. It also covers pest-control certification programs run by the Entomological Society of America, the main subdisciplines named by insect order, major entomological organizations, and a list of large insect research collections worldwide.
one_line: Overview of entomology, the scientific study of insects: its definition, history, subdisciplines, professional organizations, certifications and major research collections.
key_facts: Entomology is the scientific study of insects, a branch of zoology, from Ancient Greek 'entomon' (insect) and '-logia' (study).
Over 1.3 million insect species have been described, more than two-thirds of all known species.
Some insect species date back to around 400 million years ago.
Ulisse Aldrovandi's De Animalibus Insectis (Concerning Insect Animals) was published in 1602.
Jan Swammerdam published History of Insects, correctly describing the reproductive organs of insects and metamorphosis.
In 1705, Maria Sibylla Merian published Metamorphosis Insectorum Surinamensium about the tropical insects of Dutch Surinam.
William Kirby is widely considered the father of entomology in England and helped found the Royal Entomological Society in London in 1833.
Karl von Frisch won the 1973 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine and is listed among notable entomology figures.
E. O. Wilson, described as a twice Pulitzer Prize winner, is listed among notable entomologists.
In 1994, the Entomological Society of America launched the Associate Certified Entomologist (ACE) certification for the pest control industry.
Over 330,000 species of beetles alone are described, making identification to species very difficult even for specialists.
Automated insect species identification systems include Daisy, ABIS, SPIDA and Draw-wing.
Coleopterology is the study of beetles, Lepidopterology of moths and butterflies, and Myrmecology of ants.
The Royal Entomological Society of London was founded in 1833, one of the earliest such societies in the world.
The note describes the 'era of heroic entomology' and the later 'era of economic entomology' in the late 19th century.
